target_customer: Enterprises with large product and event data that want self service behavioral analytics
problem: Teams could not interactively explore billions of event records to understand user behavior without slow data warehouse queries.
business_model: enterprise software sold by direct sales, deployed on customer premises or cloud

founders.name: Ann Johnson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls her a former Intel executive and says Bobby Johnson is her husband.

founders.name: Bobby Johnson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch credits him with leading Facebook's Hadoop adoption, Hive, Scribe and Haystack.

founders.name: Lior Abraham
founders.background_notes: Per TechCrunch he invented Facebook's internal Scuba tool. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A custom columnar store for fast ad hoc queries over huge event tables, a research grade systems problem that the founders had solved at Facebook.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary storage and query engine plus enterprise integrations; few teams had Facebook scale infrastructure experience.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it in the years covered here; later directory entries suggest it continued independently under a new name.

market_need_then: Companies in 2013 to 2014 were collecting event data at large scale, and customers like Sony, Asana and Tinder ran the product on their own premises.

branding.brand_signature: Scuba, the internal Facebook tool the founders built on

rebrands.why: Reason not stated; directories only report the rename and the YC listing already used Scuba as the product name.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong founder credentials in press (former Facebook engineers) but the brand itself was little known and was dropped for the product name.

outcome_analysis: Interana, started by former Facebook engineers, raised 8.2 million dollars in 2014, a 20 million Series B in January 2015 and an 18 million round in November 2016 for enterprise behavioral analytics. YC marks it acquired, but no acquirer or deal was found and directories instead show a 2021 rename to Scuba Analytics, so the true exit remains unclear and funding came from top tier investors with a hard to copy engine.
notes: Exit conflict: YC directory status is Acquired but no source names an acquirer; aggregators say renamed to Scuba Analytics in January 2021 and one claims acquisition in 2018 (self contradictory). CB Insights lists a Series D on 2018-09-11 and 46.2M total across 5 rounds, single aggregator so not recorded. The 2016 round is labeled other because press releases do not name a stage. The Series A label follows a Register snippet calling the 8.2M the A round. Company site returned HTTP 402 and could not be read. No dated competitor source was found (TechCrunch 2014 names none), so the list is empty.
